st: Rinse [[0.25 cup]] bulgur in a sieve, put it in a bowl, and cover with [[0.25 cup]] of the lemon juice. Let it soak for 20 minutes to soften.
Wash the parsley well and dry it completely in a salad spinner or with towels. Wet parsley turns the salad soggy.
Pick the leaves and chop them very finely with a sharp knife, along with the mint.
Dice the tomatoes and add them to the bulgur with the green onion.
Add the parsley and mint to the bowl.
Drizzle with the remaining lemon juice, [[0.33 cup]] olive oil, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.25 tsp]] pepper and toss gently.
Taste and adjust the lemon and salt. Serve right away with romaine leaves for scooping.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Toss the torn pita with [[2 tbsp]] olive oil and [[0.5 tbsp]] sumac, spread on a baking sheet.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. Cool.
Whisk [[0.25 cup]] lemon juice, [[0.25 cup]] olive oil, [[1 clove]] garlic, [[1 tbsp]] sumac, [[1 tbsp]] pomegranate molasses and [[0.75 tsp]] salt for the dressing.
Put the lettuce, tomatoes, cucumbers, radishes, green onion, mint and parsley in a large bowl.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss.
Add the pita chips just before serving so they stay crunchy.
Rinse [[1 cup]] bulgur, soak it in cold water for 10 minutes, then squeeze it very dry.
For the filling, cook [[0.5 lb]] ground lamb in [[1 tbsp]] olive oil for 6 minutes until browned and cooked through (160°F, 71°C).
Add the diced onion, pine nuts, [[0.5 tsp]] allspice, [[0.5 tsp]] cinnamon and [[0.5 tsp]] salt and cook 4 minutes. Cool.
In a food processor, blend the lean lamb, grated onion, bulgur, [[1 tsp]] salt, [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and [[0.5 tsp]] allspice into a smooth paste, adding a few ice cubes if it gets warm.
Wet your hands and take a golf-ball-size piece of the paste. Press a hole into it with your finger to make a thin shell.
Fill with about [[1 tbsp]] filling, close the opening, and shape into an oval with pointed ends.
Chill the shaped kibbeh for 20 minutes.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil to 350°F (175°C) and fry in batches for 4 to 5 minutes until deep brown and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with yogurt or lemon.

ing: 15 oz each, drained, with liquid saved
st: Drain the chickpeas, saving the liquid. For extra smooth hummus, peel off the thin skins by hand.
Blend [[0.5 cup]] tahini and [[0.25 cup]] lemon juice in a food processor for 1 minute until pale and creamy.
Add [[2 cloves]] garlic, [[2 tbsp]] olive oil, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] cumin and blend 30 seconds.
Add half the chickpeas and blend for 1 minute, then add the rest and blend for 3 minutes until very smooth.
With the machine running, add [[3 tbsp]] ice water, or chickpea liquid, until light and creamy.
Taste and add more salt or lemon.
Spread into a shallow bowl, making a well in the middle with a spoon.
Drizzle with [[1 tbsp]] olive oil and dust with [[0.25 tsp]] paprika. Serve with pita.
Heat the oven to 450°F (230°C) and line a baking sheet with foil.
Pierce the eggplants all over with a fork. Roast on the sheet for 40 minutes, turning once, until the skins blacken and collapse.
Cool for 10 minutes, then split open and scoop the soft flesh into a colander. Discard the skin.
Let the flesh drain for 5 minutes, pressing gently to remove excess liquid.
Chop the flesh roughly and put it in a bowl.
Stir in [[3 tbsp]] tahini, [[3 tbsp]] lemon juice, [[2 cloves]] garlic, [[0.75 tsp]] salt and [[1 tbsp]] olive oil.
Taste and adjust the lemon and salt.
Spoon into a dish, drizzle with [[1 tbsp]] olive oil and top with parsley. Serve with pita.
Stir [[2.25 tsp]] yeast and [[1 tsp]] sugar into [[1.25 cups]] warm water and wait 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix in [[3.5 cups]] flour, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[2 tbsp]] olive oil. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled.
Heat the oven to 475°F (245°C) with a baking sheet inside.
Mix [[0.5 cup]] za'atar with [[0.33 cup]] olive oil to make a spreadable paste.
Divide the dough into 6 balls, roll each to a 6-inch round, and press dimples with your fingertips.
Spread the za'atar paste on the rounds, leaving a border. Scatter the cheese on some if using.
Bake each on the hot sheet for 8 to 10 minutes until puffed with golden edges.
Serve warm, folded in half or with fresh vegetables.
Cut the chicken into 1.5-inch cubes.
Whisk [[0.5 cup]] yogurt, [[0.25 cup]] lemon juice, [[3 tbsp]] olive oil, [[5 cloves]] garlic, [[1 tbsp]] paprika, [[1 tbsp]] tomato paste, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Mix the chicken into the marinade, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Thread the chicken onto the skewers, leaving small gaps.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high and oil the grates.
Cook the skewers for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until charred in spots and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Rest for 5 minutes. Serve with toum, pickles and pita.

ing: raw egg white, use pasteurized; optional
st: Peel the garlic and cut each clove in half. Remove any green sprouts, which taste bitter.
Process the garlic with [[1 tsp]] salt and the egg white in a food processor until finely minced, scraping the sides.
With the motor running, add [[1.5 cups]] oil in a very thin trickle, a few drops at a time at first.
After a few tablespoons of oil, add a little lemon juice so it keeps from splitting. Alternate oil and [[3 tbsp]] lemon juice in small amounts.
Keep going until fluffy, white, and thick like mayonnaise, about 8 minutes.
Beat in [[2 tbsp]] ice water to lighten the texture and mellow the garlic.
Scrape into a jar and refrigerate for up to 1 week. Because it contains raw egg white, use pasteurized eggs or omit it.
Put [[1 cup]] lentils and [[3 cups]] water in a pot. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes until almost tender.
Heat [[0.33 cup]] olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Add the onions with [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Cook the onions for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden brown and a little crisp. Lower the heat if they scorch.
Take out half the onions and set them aside for topping.
Stir [[0.75 cup]] rice, [[1 tsp]] cumin, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper into the lentils. Add the remaining onions and [[1 cup]] water.
Bring to a boil, cover, and cook on the lowest heat for 18 minutes until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed.
Rest covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Serve topped with the reserved onions and a drizzle of [[2 tbsp]] olive oil, with yogurt.
Make the syrup: boil [[1.5 cups]] sugar, [[1 cup]] water and [[1 tbsp]] lemon juice, then simmer 10 minutes. Stir in [[1 tbsp]] rose water and cool completely.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and butter a 9 by 13 inch pan.
Mix the walnuts, pistachios, [[0.25 cup]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] cinnamon.
Lay 1 sheet of phyllo in the pan and brush with melted butter. Repeat for 10 sheets, keeping the rest covered with a damp towel.
Sprinkle with a third of the nut mix. Add 5 more buttered sheets, then more nuts, repeating until the nuts are used up.
Finish with 10 buttered sheets on top. Brush the top with butter.
Cut into diamonds or squares all the way down with a sharp knife.
Bake for 45 minutes until deep golden.
Pour the cool syrup over the hot baklava straight from the oven. Let it soak for at least 4 hours before serving.
